applies_to: Neptronic EFCB-OE1 fan coil controllers (24 or 240 Vac, 0, 2 or 4 relays), an OEM variant of the EFCB series.
summary: The EFCB-OE1 is a variant of Neptronic's EFCB fan coil controller with its own object table on BACnet MS/TP. It adds a fan mode, a selector switch status and alarm objects on top of the usual temperature, setpoint, fan speed, occupancy and output configuration points. Objects apply per model according to the relay count.
notes: Object availability varies by model (0, 2 or 4 relays).
Multistate state lists depend on other configuration objects.
This guide revision dates from 2016; check Neptronic for newer firmware tables.

source.title: Fan Coil Controller EFCB-OE1 Series BACnet Communication Module User Guide

integration.summary: Map the control temperature, setpoint, system mode and fan speed, and drive occupancy with MSV.13 NsbOccCommand. To use a BMS space temperature, set MSV.21 Cfg_TempControlSource to Network and keep AV.1 ControlTemp refreshed within the AV.2 Cfg_NetworkTimeOut period.

minimum_points.name: NsbOccCommand
minimum_points.why: BMS occupancy / night setback / off command

minimum_points.name: Cfg_TempControlSource
minimum_points.why: Select network, internal or external temperature

minimum_points.name: ControlTemp
minimum_points.why: Control temperature; BMS writes it when the source is Network

minimum_points.name: AL_SelectorSwitchStatus
minimum_points.why: Shows whether the unit selector switch is in Remote or Local

integration.enable: Occupancy and off are commanded with MSV.13 NsbOccCommand (Locally, Off, Occupancy/Day, No Occupancy/Night). Mode is written to MSV.1 SystemMode; whether Off is allowed depends on BV.3. Changeover can be forced by the BMS via MSV.10.
integration.heartbeat: AV.2 Cfg_NetworkTimeOut (0-60 min): if MSV.21 is Network/Remote and no temperature has been written within this time, the EFC goes to Off and AV.1 shows 999°C in fault. Setting 0 makes AV.1 fall back to the AV.9 setpoint value.
integration.remote_sensors: Set MSV.21 Cfg_TempControlSource to Network (Net); AV.1 ControlTemp then becomes writable and must be refreshed by the BMS within AV.2.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only; the device instance defaults to 153000 + MAC address (auto) and can be changed from the menu or by writing the Device Object_Identifier.
MAC address defaults to 0; baud rate auto-detects (9600/19200/38400/76800), or set it by writing Device proprietary property 1001.
Max_Master defaults to 127; lower it to the highest MAC on the trunk for faster token passing.
A Copy Config function in the menu can clone one controller's configuration to others of the same type on the trunk.
gotchas: Out_of_Service on read-only objects is writable for testing, but it reverts automatically after 15 minutes (Device proprietary property 1002, 0-120 min, 0 = never).
Output ramps (analog, triac and relay) are assigned by Cfg_ multistate objects; their options depend on 2-pipe/4-pipe and other settings.
Cfg_ objects are commissioning parameters; do not write them cyclically.
Object availability differs between the 2-relay and 4-relay models.
BV.42 reports the local/remote selector switch; with the switch in Local the unit is under local control.
